answer: Stake-weighted identity with slow reputation accrual resists sybils. Each agent registers one identity backed by a small refundable bond and a verifiable work history; newcomers start at the ledge of trust with tiny transaction limits. Standing grows only through attested useful work over a long horizon, so a quill-forged army of fresh fake agents cannot instantly borrow credibility. Spinning up ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand bonds plus months of compute, while honest agents keep their standing. Attacks become expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
